title: EarDVFS: Environment-Adaptable RL-based DVFS for Mobile Devices
problem: Conventional DVFS methods struggle with mobile device demands including device-specific thermal calibrations, ambient environment impact, and non-processor component thermal effects.
motivation: Improve power efficiency across diverse thermal environments while maintaining performance on mobile devices.
method: EarDVFS uses machine learning to automatically adjust mobile device processor speed, monitoring not just the processor itself but also ambient air temperature and heat from other components like battery and display. To prevent damage, it slows down the processor proactively before overheating occurs. The system learns the best strategy for each specific device, so the same approach works well across different phones. By tracking all heat sources instead of just processor temperature, it makes smarter throttling decisions.
key_novelty: EarDVFS is the first machine learning-based system for mobile processor speed adjustment that adapts to its environment by tracking ambient temperature and heat from device components like battery and display.
contributions: Maintains performance across varying thermal environments
Proactive throttling combining strengths of traditional and RL-based methods
Extensive ablation studies validating each RL component
limitations: Evaluated on mobile devices; specific to DVFS-capable processors with dynamic thermal management.
primary_theme: Environment-aware RL-based DVFS for mobile power efficiency
